## Purpose

This guide describes a small set of review scripts used before committing and pushing substantial repository changes.

The scripts help identify:

- untracked files and likely working copies;
- references to obsolete paths or filenames;
- missing local links in QMD and Markdown pages;
- failed Quarto renders and warning messages;
- differences between authoritative public outputs and their website mirror.

The scripts are deliberately **read-only**. They produce reports but do not delete, move, copy or edit repository files. A human reviewer decides what action is appropriate.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why use reports rather than automatic cleanup?

A missing link or old filename is not always an error. It may be part of historical documentation, a generated output or a separate legacy workflow. Automatic deletion would make the process faster in roughly the same way that removing the brakes makes a car lighter.
:::

## Script locations

```text
scripts/powershell/
    check-repo-cleanliness.ps1
    check-stale-paths.ps1
    render-and-check-site.ps1

scripts/python/
    check-local-links.py
    compare-public-mirrors.py
```

Reports are written by default to:

```text
repo-review/
```

The `repo-review/` folder is temporary working material and should normally be excluded from Git.

## Requirements

The checks use software already required by the project:

- Git;
- PowerShell;
- Python 3;
- Quarto, for the render check only.

The Python scripts use only the standard library. No additional packages are required.

Run all commands from the repository root.

## 1. Review repository cleanliness

```powershell
.\scripts\powershell\check-repo-cleanliness.ps1
```

This creates:

```text
repo-review/repo-cleanliness.txt
repo-review/repo-cleanliness-candidates.csv
```

The report includes:

- the current branch;
- Git status;
- tracked and untracked file counts;
- untracked files that are not ignored;
- filenames resembling copies, backups or temporary versions;
- files larger than 10 MB.

To use a different large-file threshold:

```powershell
.\scripts\powershell\check-repo-cleanliness.ps1 -LargeFileMB 25
```

A candidate is not an instruction to delete. Check whether the file remains operationally necessary or contains material that should first be retained elsewhere.

## 2. Search for stale paths and filenames

```powershell
.\scripts\powershell\check-stale-paths.ps1
```

This creates:

```text
repo-review/stale-paths.txt
repo-review/stale-paths.csv
```

The initial rules look for references such as:

- the retired public metrics staging path;
- the private disclosure QA filename;
- legacy Step 4 and Step 5 controller names;
- old test-release identifiers;
- copied metric-page filenames.

The search rules are listed near the top of the PowerShell script. They can be updated when repository contracts change.

Review every match in context. Historical documentation may legitimately mention an old path.

## 3. Check local links

```powershell
python .\scripts\python\check-local-links.py
```

This creates:

```text
repo-review/local-links.csv
repo-review/local-links.md
```

Each local link is classified as:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `exists` | The linked file currently exists |
| `generated` | The final HTML is absent, but a matching QMD or Markdown source exists |
| `missing` | No local target or obvious Quarto source was found |

The script ignores external web, email and telephone links. It recognises that a link to `page.html` may be generated from `page.qmd`.

A non-zero command exit indicates that at least one missing link was found. The reports are still created.

## 4. Render the Quarto site

```powershell
.\scripts\powershell\render-and-check-site.ps1
```

This runs a complete render from the `site/` project and creates:

```text
repo-review/quarto-render.log
repo-review/quarto-render-summary.txt
```

The summary records:

- the render start and finish time;
- the Quarto exit code;
- overall success or failure;
- log lines containing terms such as `warning`, `error`, `not found` or `missing`.

A successful exit code does not make every warning harmless. Review the summary and relevant portions of the full log.

The script does not remove the Quarto cache before rendering. Cache removal should remain an explicit troubleshooting action rather than a routine side effect.

## 5. Compare public outputs with the website mirror

```powershell
python .\scripts\python\compare-public-mirrors.py
```

By default, the script compares:

```text
outputs/public/
site/downloads/files/
```

It creates:

```text
repo-review/public-mirror-comparison.csv
repo-review/public-mirror-summary.txt
```

Files are classified as:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `identical` | Present in both locations with the same SHA-256 checksum |
| `different` | Present in both locations but contents differ |
| `public_only` | Present only in the authoritative public location |
| `mirror_only` | Present only in the website mirror |

The comparison covers all public outputs, including briefings and metrics. Alternative paths can be supplied when a narrower comparison is needed:

```powershell
python .\scripts\python\compare-public-mirrors.py `
    --public outputs/public/metrics/cvd/burden `
    --mirror site/downloads/files/metrics/cvd/burden
```

A difference is not repaired automatically. Re-run the approved publication process rather than manually copying individual files where possible.

## Recommended review sequence

Run the checks in this order:

```powershell
.\scripts\powershell\check-repo-cleanliness.ps1
.\scripts\powershell\check-stale-paths.ps1
python .\scripts\python\check-local-links.py
.\scripts\powershell\render-and-check-site.ps1
python .\scripts\python\compare-public-mirrors.py
```

Then review Git itself:

```powershell
git status
git diff --stat
git diff
```

## Interpreting the findings

Use the reports to place findings into four groups:

1. **Correct now**: confirmed broken links, stale public paths or accidental working copies.
2. **Retain**: active operational files and intentional historical documentation.
3. **Investigate**: uncertain legacy files, generated outputs or separate briefing pathways.
4. **Regenerate**: files that should be recreated by Stata, Quarto or the publication workflow rather than edited manually.

Do not treat zero findings as proof that the repository is perfect. The scripts check defined technical conditions; they do not assess whether prose is current, whether a page is still useful or whether the publication architecture is sensible.

## After making corrections

Re-run all five checks. A repository is ready for the normal commit process when:

- unexplained untracked files have been resolved;
- stale-path matches are understood;
- missing local links have been corrected or documented;
- the Quarto render completes successfully;
- public and website-mirror differences are expected and explained;
- `git diff` contains only intended changes.

The reports themselves are working artefacts. They should not normally be included in the commit.
